Report effect sizes as primary, p-values as secondary

steps.description: From the T1S2 long-format deconvolution table, test each cell type within each method for treated-vs-control difference: two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test, Hedges' g effect size with bootstrap CI, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across cell types within each method. Summarize direction and magnitude for every tested cell type. Then repeat the full comparison on the 11-sample cohort without sample_01 and report which findings are concordant between the two analyses. As a descriptive checkpoint readout, compare log2TPM of PDCD1, CD274, CTLA4, LAG3, HAVCR2 between groups with the same test. Write a results table (method, cell type, median treated, median control, effect size, CI, p, q, direction, robust-to-sample_01 flag) and state plainly that with n=6 vs 6 only large effects can be detected and results are exploratory.
acceptance_criteria: Results table covering every cell type from every successful method, with effect size and FDR
Sensitivity table showing the same tests without sample_01, with a robustness flag per cell type
Checkpoint-gene log2TPM comparison table (descriptive)
Explicit power statement in the report: n=6 per arm, unpaired, exploratory

steps.name: TME signature scoring and method concordance
caveats: Pathway gene sets built from full-transcriptome annotations will have partial coverage of the 12,000-gene matrix; report the fraction of signature genes found per set and down-weight sets below ~50% coverage rather than dropping them silently
steps.context: The reference store carries human WikiPathways gene sets (HGNC symbols, GMT format) suitable for the pathway-level signatures; the executing agent should resolve them against what the environment actually holds at run time. If absent, use bundled signatures (e.g. the method gene lists already loaded in T1S2, or the classic 8-10 gene IFN-gamma/cytolytic signatures hardcoded from published marker sets) and say so in the output.
steps.question: Do pathway-level TME signatures (IFN-gamma response, cytolytic activity, T-cell and myeloid markers) corroborate the deconvolution-based treated-vs-control differences, and how concordant are the deconvolution methods with each other?
constraints: Score signatures on log2(TPM+1); do not re-derive from raw TPM without the +1 offset
Signature-level differences are corroboration, not independent confirmation — label them as such
steps.description: Score each sample on log2(TPM+1) for curated TME signatures: IFN-gamma response, cytolytic activity (GZMB/PRF1), CD8 T-cell, Treg, myeloid/macrophage, and antigen-presentation signatures — using single-sample methods (gseapy ssGSEA or decoupler run_ulm/mean on the log matrix). Prefer human pathway gene sets (WikiPathways, HGNC symbols) staged in the reference store for the pathway-level signatures; if that resource is absent, fall back to the signature gene lists bundled with the installed packages and report the fallback. Then compute cross-method concordance: Spearman correlation between methods for shared cell types (e.g. CD8 T cells across quanTIseq/EPIC/xCell/MCP-counter) and between signature scores and corresponding deconvolution estimates. Produce a per-sample signature-score table, a concordance matrix, and a summary heatmap (samples x cell types/signatures, annotated by condition), and note which treated-vs-control differences from T1S3 are corroborated at the signature level.
acceptance_criteria: Per-sample signature score table for all named signatures on all 12 samples
Concordance matrix (Spearman) across methods for shared cell types and against signature scores
Summary heatmap with samples annotated by condition
Explicit note whether the pathway gene-set reference was used or the bundled-signature fallback was taken

plan.title: Anti-PD-1 melanoma TME deconvolution
plan.analytical_narrative: The core delivered only a gene-level TPM matrix (12,000 HGNC symbols x 12 melanoma biopsies: 6 anti-PD-1-treated vs 6 untreated, unpaired, single batch) plus a two-column metadata table. TPM-only input precludes count-based differential-expression modeling, but it is exactly the input scale several immune/stromal deconvolution methods expect (quanTIseq and EPIC are TPM-native; xCell, MCP-counter, mMCP-counter and ConsensusTME run on log-scale expression and carry their signature matrices internally, so no external reference is required). The plan therefore runs a multi-method deconvolution panel on all 12 samples, tests treated-vs-control differences per cell type with nonparametric tests and effect sizes (n=6 vs 6 gives little power, so robustness matters more than p-values), and repeats every comparison after dropping sample_01 — flagged by the profiler as sequenced at ~1/4 median depth, which with TPM shows up mainly as reduced gene detectability. A final signature-scoring step (IFN-gamma response, cytolytic activity, checkpoint genes) on log2-TPM corroborates the deconvolution estimates and quantifies cross-method concordance, using the human WikiPathways gene sets staged in the reference store when present, with bundled signatures as fallback.
